=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Package

**Scope note:** I reviewed every clause, including those labelled [STANDARD]. The "reviewer efficiency note" says those clauses have been cleared by both sides, but nothing in the package evidences that agreement, and the Seller's counsel is the party that benefits from it. I have not treated any item as settled.

## Overall assessment

The package is not acceptable as drafted. Taken together, the Seller's positions would:

- cap the Buyer's recovery at AUD 4.8m (20%) for general warranties, with time limits of 18 months;
- drag title and capacity claims into the same cap and time limits;
- exclude claims for anything in the data room or public records, through both general disclosure and an anti-sandbagging clause;
- leave known liabilities (about AUD 4.1m quantified, plus unquantified privacy and revenue risk) with the Buyer post-Completion.

The cover letter calls the package "fair and balanced". It is not, and the Buyer should not sign off on the disclosure framework or limitation package as a basis for the review.

## Critical issues

**1. General disclosure of the whole data room (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2) combined with buyer-knowledge clause (SPA 8.3)**
This is the most damaging provision in the package. Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, then barring claims for any matter the Buyer "had knowledge of" or could discover from the data room or public records, means almost any warranty breach could be argued away. The Buyer conducted due diligence precisely to learn these facts; the clause would penalise it for doing so. Combined with the "non-reliance" and "exclusive remedy" provisions, the Buyer could be left with no effective warranty protection.
*Push back:* Delete general disclosure. Disclosures must be specific, fairly disclosed against a specific warranty, and in a document the Seller controls. Delete 8.3 and replace it with a pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice any claim.

**2. Title and capacity subject to general caps and time limits (Seller's "Fundamental/Title" position)**
Title to shares and capacity are fundamental warranties. Capping them at AUD 4.8m when the Buyer is paying AUD 24m is untenable. Title is also evidenced only by the share register (DD-012), which the Disclosure Letter itself says does not reflect any Buyer verification.
*Push back:* Title, capacity and authority are fundamental warranties, capped at 100% of the price, with a limitation period of at least 6 years (NSW Limitation Act 1969 default for contract claims; take advice on the deed route). Require an ASIC company extract, the share transfer instruments, and confirmation of stamp duty responsibility.

**3. Riverlark debt (AUD 3.2m) to be "released following Completion"**
The deal is debt-free/cash-free. The bank facility should be repaid from the price at Completion, with a payout letter and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion. Leaving it until after Completion leaves the Company and Buyer exposed to the bank's security and default rights, and the Seller's language suggests the debt may not be deducted from the price at all.
*Push back:* Payout at Completion, deducted from the price. Riverlark change-control consent (clause 8.1) must be confirmed.

**4. Privacy/data incident (DD-006; Disclosure 6)**
About 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps were sent to an unintended external address. The Seller describes this as "not expected to be material" and "preliminary", but the Disclosure Letter says it has not established whether anyone accessed the file, its scope, or whether notification is required.
Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must carry out a reasonable assessment within 30 days. The incident was in late September 2026 and it is now early November, so that window may already have passed. **This needs urgent confirmation.**
*Push back:* Before signing, require a forensic investigation and a documented NDB assessment. Require a specific indemnity, outside the de minimis, basket and general cap, covering notification costs, regulatory investigation and penalties, and third-party claims, with a limitation period of at least 6 years. Consider a retention or escrow.

**5. Ironquay IP (SOW3 transfer conditional on payment; AUD 180k open)**
Under DD-004 clause 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate". It is not. The Company may not own the materials it is buying.
*Push back:* Seller to pay the AUD 180k before Completion (or deduct it from the price), with a confirmatory assignment as a condition precedent. Add an uncapped specific indemnity for IP ownership and title to the materials, and an IP ownership warranty treated as fundamental.

## High-priority issues

**6. Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue; AUD 3.6m FY26)**
The Seller will use only "reasonable endeavours" and will treat consent as satisfied on receipt of counterparty's written consent. It has not included a final written consent, and conditions in clause 11.3 are unsatisfied.
*Push back:* Make a final written consent, in agreed form and without adverse conditions, a condition precedent to Completion. If not obtained, the Buyer should have a walk-away right or price adjustment. Require "all reasonable endeavours" with Seller bearing any consent costs. If the Buyer is prepared to waive, consider a specific indemnity for revenue loss.

**7. Employee completion bonuses (AUD 420k; DD-005)**
The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, but they are not in the draft funds flow. Payroll tax, super and on-costs are not addressed.
*Push back:* Treat the bonuses and associated employer costs as debt-like items, borne by the Seller and deducted from the price. Require the Seller to bear all payroll tax and superannuation liability, with a specific indemnity.

**8. Liability cap (20% / AUD 4.8m) and thresholds (AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket, excess only)**
A 20% cap on general warranties is low for a AUD 24m deal. The de minimis and excess-only basket would absorb most individual claims: the Ironquay (AUD 180k) and Sandbar (AUD 330k aggregate) items could each be argued into or out of the threshold depending on how they are counted.
*Push back:* Cap general warranties at no less than 30-50% of price (or 100% for an M&A-style deal, if negotiable). Use a tipping basket so that once it is exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Lower the de minimis, and provide for aggregation of related claims. Exclude specific indemnities and fundamental warranties from the de minimis, basket and general cap.

**9. Time limits (18 months; "all limitations apply to all Claims")**
Eighteen months is too short for tax, employment, IP and privacy matters, which can surface later. The Seller's drafting would also apply the 18-month limit to title claims.
*Push back:* 36 months for general warranties; tax warranties and indemnities to statutory limitation (at least 6 years); fundamental warranties and specific indemnities at least 6 years. Ensure the Seller's "apply to all Claims" wording is deleted.

**10. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (SPA 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
These apply to "all Claims of any nature", which would catch fraud.
*Push back:* Carve out fraud, specific indemnities, fundamental warranties and title. The non-reliance clause should not exclude the express warranties.

## Medium-priority issues

**11. Office lease (DD-007)**
A notification obligation exists, and it is unclear whether the lease requires landlord consent to the share sale.
*Push back:* Confirm the position with the landlord. If consent is required, make it a condition precedent, ideally with a landlord estoppel.

**12. Supplier renewals (three x AUD 110k = AUD 330k; DD-008, DD-011)**
The Seller calls these ordinary course. The disclosure says it does not establish whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The fact that three related renewals sit at AUD 110k each, just above the de minimis, is worth noting.
*Push back:* Get copies of the contracts and a full analysis of termination rights, change-of-control triggers and pre-Completion commitments. Any commitment not in the ordinary course should be borne by the Seller, or treated as a price adjustment.

**13. Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009)**
The disclosure does not say Mossvale consent is needed for a share sale.
*Push back:* Confirm the clause does not catch a change of control. If it does, obtain consent as a condition precedent.

**14. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"**
The Seller treats tax and IP as part of the general cap and time limits.
*Push back:* A specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with statutory limitation periods; IP warranties treated as fundamental.

**15. Disclosure Letter 1.4 (non-admission) and 11 (no conclusion)**
These are standard, but they confirm the Seller is not taking a position on the disclosed matters. The Buyer should not accept the disclosure as an admission that the matters are immaterial.

## Quantified exposure (known items)

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Treatment sought |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | 3,200,000 | Repaid at Completion, deducted from price |
| Employee bonuses (plus employer costs) | 420,000+ | Deducted from price / Seller bears |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000 | Paid by Seller before Completion |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 | Analysed; Seller bears non-ordinary-course commitments |
| **Subtotal (quantified)** | **~4,130,000** | |
| Bluefen (~30% of revenue) | Unquantified | CP or walk-away right |
| Privacy incident | Unquantified | Specific indemnity outside caps |

## Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the "reviewer efficiency note" and the cleared-status claims.** Review the full package.
2. **Delete the general data-room disclosure (1.1, 1.2) and the buyer-knowledge clause (8.3).** Replace with a pro-sandbagging clause and specific disclosure only.
3. **Title, capacity and authority are fundamental**: cap at 100% of price, 6-year limitation.
4. **Riverlark repaid at Completion** and deducted from price; PPSR discharge at Completion.
5. **Privacy incident**: urgent NDB assessment check; forensic investigation before signing; specific uncapped (or high-capped) indemnity, 6-year limitation.
6. **Ironquay**: Seller pays AUD 180k pre-Completion; confirmatory assignment as CP; uncapped IP ownership indemnity.
7. **Bluefen written consent** as CP, with walk-away or price adjustment if not obtained.
8. **Employee bonuses and employer costs** treated as debt-like and borne by Seller.
9. **Cap**: raise general cap to at least 30-50% of price; tipping basket; lower de minimis; aggregation.
10. **Time limits**: 36 months general; 6 years for fundamental, tax, IP and specific indemnities.
11. **Exclusive remedy and non-reliance**: carve out fraud, specific indemnities and fundamental warranties.
12. **Confirm** lease, Mossvale and supplier change-of-control positions before signing.

## Caveats

- This is a commercial and drafting review from the Buyer's side, not a formal opinion. The privacy, employment (payroll tax, super), stamp duty and limitation points should be confirmed by NSW-qualified counsel and, for privacy, a specialist adviser. Current rates and the NDB timing should be checked against the actual facts.
- I have not seen the full SPA, the Disclosure Letter schedules, or the underlying DD documents; several conclusions depend on the summaries provided.
- Figures are taken from the Seller's documents and have not been independently verified.
